title.zh: 去八百英里外求援：象岛上的一次名单与取舍
title.en: Eight Hundred Miles for Help: A Crew List and Its Trade-offs on Elephant Island

dek.zh: 足额口粮只够五个星期，一条小船，六个名额。队长要说服全队走一条危险极大的路，还要否掉带病号上船的提议，并在开船前把整支队伍交到留守者手里。
dek.en: Full rations for five weeks, one small boat, six places. The leader had to talk the whole party into a voyage whose perils were extreme, veto a proposal to take a sick man along, and hand the stranded party over to the man staying behind before the boat pulled away.

paras.zh: 象岛上，口粮按足额只够全队吃五个星期，减量可以撑三个月，或许还能靠海兽补一些，但队长不敢把信心全押在这上面：海滩上的海兽似乎都走了，冬天近了。存量里有三只海豹和两张半带脂肪的兽皮，燃料主要靠脂肪。初步估量形势后，队长决定全队每天只吃一顿热食。
paras.en: On Elephant Island the food would last the whole party five weeks at full ration. Cut back, it could be spread over three months, and would probably be supplemented to some extent by seals and sea-elephants — but the leader dared not count on that with full confidence. The animals seemed to have deserted the beach and winter was near. Their stocks included three seals and two and a half skins with the blubber attached, and they were mainly dependent on blubber for fuel. After a preliminary survey of the situation, he decided the party must be limited to one hot meal a day.

paras.zh: 除了粮食，人的状况也令人担心。艰苦与风寒在队伍身上留下了痕迹，几名队员的健康和精神状况令人深感不安；一名队员的双脚在乘船途中冻伤，伤势很糟，两位医生担心必须动手术。
paras.en: Beyond the food, the men's condition was also a worry. Privation and exposure had left their mark on the party, and the health and mental condition of several men were causing serious anxiety. One man's feet, frostbitten during the boat journey, were in a bad way, and the two doctors feared an operation would be necessary.

paras.zh: 摆在面前的出路只有一条：派人乘小船出海求援，而且不能拖。记述里写这一句时没有回旋余地——「That conclusion was forced upon me」，这个结论是被逼出来的。
paras.en: One way out remained: take a boat for help, and do it now. The account leaves no room to maneuver — "That conclusion was forced upon me". The conclusion was forced on him.

paras.zh: 求援的去处是南乔治亚。它在八百多英里以外，但位于西风带内，东岸任何一个捕鲸站都可以指望找到捕鲸人；只要海上没有冰、小船撑得过那些巨浪，一队人乘船可望完成航行，并在一个月之内带着援助返回。
paras.en: The destination was South Georgia. It lay over eight hundred miles off, but inside the belt of the west winds, and whalers could be counted on at any of the whaling stations on its east coast. Provided the sea was clear of ice and the boat survived the great seas, a boat party might make the voyage and be back with relief within a month.

paras.zh: 出海的风险明摆着。队长算过最坏情形：这趟冒险不会给留在岛上的人增加任何风险，冬天要吃饭的嘴也少了；船上只带六人一个月的口粮——「for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under」，一个月到不了南乔治亚，就是死路。还有一条让他格外看重的考虑：象岛上根本不会有任何搜寻队来找他们。
paras.en: The hazards of the ocean were plain, but the leader had priced the worst case. At worst the venture would add nothing to the risks of the men left on the island — there would be fewer mouths to feed through the winter — and the boat needed no more than a month's provisions for six, "for if we did not make South Georgia in that time we were sure to go under". And one consideration weighed with him: there was no chance at all of any search being made for them on Elephant Island.

paras.zh: 这件事必须向全队讲清楚。记述写明这个案子需要详细论证，因为所有人都知道航程的危险是极端的，风险只由援助的急迫需要来辩护。五月中，合恩角以南的海域被认为是世界上最暴虐的风暴水域，天气不稳，天色阴沉，大风几乎不停。一种解释是：他没有把出海说成上策，只说成不得已。
paras.en: The case had to be argued to the whole party in some detail, since everyone knew the journey's perils were extreme, and the risk was justified only by their urgent need of assistance. In mid-May the ocean south of Cape Horn is known to be the most tempestuous storm-swept area of water in the world: unsettled weather, dull overcast skies, gales almost unceasing. One reading is that he did not present the voyage as the best option, only the necessary one.

paras.zh: 谁去谁留，从两个要求随行的人说起。Worsley 和 Wild 都意识到必须出海，都要求随行；队长当场告诉 Wild 他必须留下，靠他把队伍拢住，并交代万一求援失败，春季带人去 Deception Island。带 Worsley 的理由写得很实在：队长对他的定位又快又准评价极高，尤其在困难情况下能迅速测出并算出船位。
paras.en: Who went and who stayed began with two men who asked to come. Worsley and Wild both realized the attempt must be made, and both asked to accompany him. The leader told Wild at once that he must stay — to hold the party together during the absence and, if the rescue failed, to take the men to Deception Island in the spring. His reason for taking Worsley was practical: "a very high opinion of his accuracy and quickness as a navigator, and especially in the snapping and working out of positions in difficult circumstances".

paras.zh: 还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时老老实实写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。Crean 原本被安排留在岛上当 Wild 的帮手，他恳求随行，与 Wild 商量之后，队长答应带上他。挑人的标准也摆在明处：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。
paras.en: Four more were needed. He called for volunteers while admitting, honestly, that he already knew his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The criteria were stated openly: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.

paras.zh: 有人提议把双脚冻伤的 Blackborrow 带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺在舱底、动弹不得的人，熬不过必定会遇到的坏天气。
paras.en: One proposal was to take Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not be expected to survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.

paras.zh: 名单最后定为 Worsley、Crean、McNeish、McCarthy、Vincent 和队长本人六人。队长把木匠叫来，请他想办法让小船更耐风浪；木匠先问自己是不是随行的人，听说「Yes」显得相当高兴。他年过五十，身体不算好。
paras.en: The list closed at six: Worsley, Crean, McNeish, McCarthy, Vincent, and the leader himself. The leader called the carpenter and asked whether he could do anything to make the boat more seaworthy; the carpenter's first question was whether he was going along, and hearing "Yes," he seemed quite pleased. He was over fifty and not altogether fit.

paras.zh: 拼凑出来的东西很简陋，但足以给一层帆布覆罩打底。帆布冻得硬邦邦，只能先裁好，再在脂肪炉上一英尺一英尺地烤开，才能缝成覆罩，最后钉好、拧紧。覆罩装上后确实给了小船一层安全的样子，可队长心里不踏实，觉得它「bore a strong likeness to stage scenery」——看着像花岗石墙，其实不过是帆布和板条。事后证明，这层覆罩确实顶用。
paras.en: What was put together was a patched-up affair, but it provided a base for a canvas covering. The canvas came frozen stiff; it had to be cut and then thawed over the blubber stove foot by foot before it could be sewn into a cover, then nailed and screwed into position. The cover did lend the boat an appearance of safety, but the leader felt uneasy that "it bore a strong likeness to stage scenery" — a wall that looks like granite and is in fact no better than canvas and lath. As events proved, the covering served its purpose well.

paras.zh: 浮冰随时可能合拢。决定做出后，队长用当天余下的时间检查船、装备和物资，并与 Worsley、Wild 商量计划。在象岛坚实陆地上的最后一夜又冷又不舒服。开船前，队长乘小艇上岸，与留守并全权指挥的 Wild 作最后交代：交代万一求援失败他该怎么做，同时几乎把整个局面和行动、决定的范围都交给 Wild 自行判断，「I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment」，并告诉他把队伍托付给他，随后向众人道别。升帆解缆向东北而去时，留在岸上的人在海边站成可怜的一小群，背后是岛上冷硬的高地，脚下的海在翻涌；他们挥手，喊了三声欢呼。
paras.en: The pack might close at any time. With that decision made, the leader spent the rest of the day looking over the boat, gear and stores, and discussing plans with Worsley and Wild. The last night on the solid ground of Elephant Island was cold and uncomfortable. Before casting off, the leader went ashore for a final word with Wild, who remained in full command: directions for what to do if no help came, and then, in his words, "I practically left the whole situation and scope of action and decision to his own judgment". He told Wild he trusted the party to him and said goodbye to the men. With the jib set and the painter cut, they stood away to the north-east. Those left behind made a pathetic little group on the beach, grim heights at their backs and the sea seething at their feet — but they waved and gave three hearty cheers.

paras.zh: 船上的日子从细节开始磨人。做饭要三个人：一人护灯，两人护铝锅——锅得随时从炉子上提开，免得船一晃出事；灯也要挡水，浪花不断从船头打过来，那层覆罩并不防水。人都挤在覆罩底下，贴着箱子和压舱物找角度躺跪；虽不舒服，但没有这层覆罩根本没法做饭。出海第六天早上，船被夜里结的冰压得失去弹性，不再随浪抬起，像根圆木。先扔掉冻在船侧的备用桨，留两支靠岸用；再扔掉两条湿透冻硬的毛皮睡袋（各约四十磅）。值下班的有三个人，与其用体温去焐冻硬的睡袋，不如钻进别人刚腾出的湿睡袋。剩下四条，三条在用，一条留给有人彻底垮掉时应急。
paras.en: Life aboard wore men down in details. Cooking needed three: one to hold the lamp, two to guard the aluminium pot, which had to be lifted clear of the Primus stove whenever a lurch threatened disaster; the lamp needed shielding from water, since spray came over the bows and the flimsy decking was by no means watertight. All of it happened in the cramped space beneath the decking, men lying or kneeling and wedging themselves against cases and ballast — uncomfortable, though without the decking they could not have cooked at all. On the morning of the sixth day the boat lost her resiliency and stopped rising to the seas, weighed down by ice that had formed overnight: more log than boat. The spare oars, frozen to her sides, went overboard, two kept for inshore work. Two fur sleeping-bags followed — soaked through, probably forty pounds each, frozen stiff. With three men in the watch below, it was better to turn into a wet bag just vacated by another man than to thaw a frozen one with body heat. Four bags were left: three in use, one held back in case a man broke down for good.

paras.zh: 有一天上午 11 点前后，缆绳断了，海锚丢失，船突然横落进浪谷，向下风漂去。那是不必冒险在大风中升帆也能让船头顶浪的唯一手段，连同宝贵的绳子都找不回来，只能敲掉帆上的冰，升帆赌它撑得住。航程中一次测算显示：已走 380 多英里，接近南乔治亚的一半。看样子能撑过去。
paras.en: About 11 a.m. one day the painter parted and the sea-anchor went — the only means of keeping the boat's head up to the seas without the risk of hoisting sail in a gale, lost along with the valuable rope. She suddenly fell off into the trough of the sea and drifted to leeward. They beat the ice off the frozen canvas and hoisted it, trusting it to hold. One reckoning showed over 380 miles done, getting on for half-way to South Georgia. It looked as though they were going to get through.

paras.zh: 航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。Vincent 在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比 McCarthy 更能吃苦，而 McCarthy 没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害；队长不肯增加配给，有人恳求预支第二天的水，也被拒绝：万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。
paras.en: At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst; the leader would not raise the allowance or let anyone draw against the morrow's, however he was begged — should the wind turn unfavourable, it might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure.

paras.zh: 把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，失败就是失败，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。作者推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。
paras.en: Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they failed, they failed. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. The author infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.

paras.zh: 拒绝病号上船那一条，读起来最不舒服，但记录里给的是存活推断，不是道德立场：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺舱底的人熬不过坏天气。作者推断，这种取舍的难处不在决定本身，而在它必须给出理由——有人提了建议，被否掉了，记述里写明了否决的理由。原文没有说这些理由是否当众向全队讲过；若是讲过，代价至少由全队一起看见，而不是由某个被悄悄放下的人独自承担，但这只是未经证实的推测。
paras.en: The refusal of the sick man is the least comfortable paragraph to read, yet the record offers survival reasoning rather than a moral stance: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom would not survive the heavy weather. The author infers that the difficulty of such a trade-off lies less in the decision itself than in having to give reasons for it: a proposal was made and vetoed, and the account sets down why. The original does not say whether those reasons were put to the whole party; if they were, the cost would at least have been visible to everyone rather than borne by one person quietly set aside — but that is an unverified conjecture.

paras.zh: 还有一处值得留意：一边征求志愿者，一边心里早有人选。作者提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式；但记录里的顺序——先说清危险和理由，再征求意见，最后落名单——可能让名单更像共识而不是指派。这只是一种解释，原文没有说明他为什么这样安排。
paras.en: One more detail catches the eye: he asked for volunteers while already knowing his choices. One alternative would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. But the sequence in the record — spell out the danger and the reasons, ask for willingness, then settle the list — may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. That is only one reading; the original gives no reason for the arrangement.

paras.zh: 今天，资源有限、外部不会主动来救的小团队会遇到同一类问题。一个只有几个人的偏远工作站，补给只够再撑一段时间，通讯断了，下一班补给不知何时到：是全员留下硬撑，还是派人冒险出去求援？先算最坏情形——出去的人会不会让留下的人更糟？定量能砍到什么程度，又能把可撑的时间延长多少？
paras.en: Small teams short of resources, with no outside rescue coming, face the same question. A remote station of a few people, supplies good for another stretch of time, communications down, the next resupply date unknown: does everyone stay and endure, or does someone go out and risk seeking help? Start with the worst case: does sending people out make matters worse for those who stay? How far can rations be cut, and how much longer would that let them hold out?

paras.zh: 第二类问题是临走前怎么交班。负责人要同时交出两样东西：失败时的后手——到某个时点没消息就换方案；以及现场的判断范围。只交代步骤不给判断权，留守的人会事事等消息；只说“你看着办”却不讲失败的下场，责任就悬在半空。
paras.en: The second problem is the handover before departure. A leader must hand over two things at once: the fallback if the attempt fails — no word by a certain point, then switch plans — and the scope of judgment on the ground. Steps without judgment leave those behind waiting for instructions on everything; "use your own judgment" without spelling out what failure looks like leaves responsibility hanging in mid-air.

paras.zh: 这套记录只有当事人一个史源，是他事后写下的第一人称自述。文中的对话都带有记述性质：把队伍托付给 Wild 的那句交代、Crean 恳求随行，都未必是逐字原话。队长自述看队员时信心在增加，那是回忆中的自我描述，不是当时可核实的心理记录。
paras.en: This record rests on exactly one historical source: a first-person account written after the fact by one of those involved. Its dialogue is reported, not transcribed — the words entrusting the party to Wild, Crean's plea for a place in the boat — and need not be verbatim. The leader's statement that his confidence grew as he looked at the men is retrospective self-description, not a verifiable record of his state of mind at the time.

paras.zh: 还有两处要留白。Vincent 为什么垮掉，队长自己说难以解释，本文不替他补心理。所引片段未给公元年份，这里不做换算；正文的天数只保留原文明确写出的出海第六天，月份照原文；距离、口粮、水的数字都照原文：八百多英里、三百八十多英里、半品脱。原文是扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文写法。
paras.en: Two blanks stay blank. Why Vincent collapsed, the leader himself says he could not easily account for, and this piece supplies no psychology for him. The quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied here; the only day count kept in the text is the sixth day out, which the original states explicitly, and the month follows the original; distances, rations and water figures follow the original: over eight hundred miles, over three hundred and eighty miles, half a pint. The source is a scanned, text-recognized print, with occasional garbled words; quotations follow it as printed.

scenario.zh: 五个人的小团队，账上只够发四个月工资，产品不上线就没有收入；其中两个人是唯一能对外谈事的人。要不要派人出去找钱、找渠道，谁去谁留？
scenario.en: A five-person team with only four months of payroll left in the bank and no revenue until the product ships; two of the five are the only ones who can negotiate with the outside world. Do you send someone out to raise money and open channels — and who goes, who stays?

question.zh: 当所有选项都很糟时，什么样的最坏情形算法能让人自愿跟从？把它讲得太清楚，会不会反而没人敢去？
question.en: When every option is bad, what kind of worst-case arithmetic makes people willing to follow? And does spelling it out too clearly risk frightening everyone off the attempt?

assumptions.zh: 团队五人；现金够四个月；外部不会主动注资；两人有对外谈判能力，另外三人维持产品；失败意味着全部投入归零。
assumptions.en: Five people; cash for four months; no outside funding will arrive uninvited; two can negotiate externally while three keep the product moving; failure means losing everything invested.

steps.zh: 先算最坏情形：出去的人不增加留守者的开支，反而少一份开销；给出去的人定明确的时限与物资上限（例如一个月、只带够一个月开销的钱），超时即默认失败；把“风险只由急迫需要来辩护”这一点说清楚；公开征求意愿，但事先想好人选；离开前交代失败时的后手，并把现场判断权交给留守负责人。
steps.en: Compute the worst case first: the person who goes adds nothing to the burn of those who stay, and in fact removes one salary's worth of cost. Set a hard time limit and a supply cap for the trip (say, a month, carrying only a month of expenses), with silence past the deadline counted as failure. State plainly that the risk is justified only by the urgent need for help. Ask for volunteers in the open, with the choices already thought through. Before leaving, hand over the fallback for failure, and delegate real judgment to the person staying behind.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的一种替代：不派人出去，全员接零活维持现金流。好处是短期内不分散人力，代价是没有人去打开外部通道，四个月后仍然没有援手。
alternative.en: One alternative the author raises: send nobody out, and have everyone take contract work to keep cash flowing. The gain is that no one is pulled off the front line in the short term; the cost is that no one opens an outside channel, and after four months there is still no help.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全文只有当事人一个史源（其事后的第一人称自述）；对话与心理均为记述性内容，未必逐字、不可核实；天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天，月份照原文，所引片段未给公元年份，不做换算；距离、口粮、水的数字照原文写法；原文为扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文。
uncertainty_note.en: The whole piece rests on a single source — one participant's first-person account written afterwards. Dialogue and psychology are reported rather than transcribed, need not be verbatim, and cannot be verified; the only day count used is the sixth day out, as stated in the original, months follow the original, and the quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied; distances, rations and water figures follow the original wording; the source is a scanned print in OCR, with individual words occasionally garbled, and quotations follow it as printed.
